terra.problem: The passage does not say the family started with one old man and his sons or that they filled the region.
The text does not establish that nobody scattered or lost anything.
The claim that they are not packing a single bag goes beyond what the verse says.
The promise to Jacob's descendants does not establish that Jacob will not live in the land.
The explanation attributes the identification of Ephrath as Bethlehem to Jacob, but the text gives it as a parenthetical note.
The passage says Rachel was buried beside the road, but does not say she was not buried in a cave.
The text does not say Jacob asked who the boys were because of his poor eyesight.
Calling it a moment with just a grandfather and his grandsons leaves Joseph out, though he is present.
The explanation is generic and ends with filler rather than a distinctive Papa Dorin observation.
The explanation simply repeats the verse and its order, without a distinctive Papa Dorin voice.
The text does not say Joseph points at Manasseh.
Saying it goes the other way suggests Manasseh will serve Ephraim. Israel says Ephraim will be greater, not that Manasseh will serve him.
The explanation is flat and repetitive; the final sentence merely restates that sheep are not land.
